title: Optimization of the Treatment Pathway for Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation (TAVI)
summary:
The ASPIRE study is a prospective, non-interventional observational study with a retrospective comparison cohort (pre-post design). Its objective is to evaluate the implementation of a standardized, evidence-based, and digitally supported treatment pathway for patients with severe, symptomatic aortic valve stenosis undergoing elective transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) at the Deutsches Herzzentrum der Charité (DHZC), Campus Virchow-Klinikum.
The optimized treatment pathway integrates structured pre-admission preparation, interdisciplinary process standards spanning the entire TAVI treatment course, as well as digital patient information and support.
The study is part of the EU-funded EuroHeartPath consortium and serves to evaluate the implementation of best practice care models in routine clinical practice.
All diagnostic and therapeutic measures are performed as part of routine clinical care, independent of study participation. The only study-specific activities involved are structured data collection, surveys, and scientific analyses.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- planned elective TAVI at the DHZC
- ability to consent
- written consent
Exclusion criteria:
- Age < 18 years
- Urgent or emergency procedures
- Severe cognitive impairment
- Legal guardianship
- Life expectancy < 1 year
- Insufficient language proficiency to independently utilize study information and standardized questionnaires
